title: Algebraic residues after adjoining an algebraic coefficient field
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative domain and $L$ a field with compatible $R$- and $\operatorname{Frac}(R)$-algebra structures, where $L/\operatorname{Frac}(R)$ is algebraic. Let $X$ be an affine scheme [def-pc-scheme], [def-weil-affine-spectrum], let $E,B$ be commutative rings, and let $a:\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)\to E$, $r:R\to\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)$, $b:E\to B$, and $h:L\to B$ be ring maps. Assume $\operatorname{Spec}(a)$ is étale and $b\circ a\circ r=h\circ(R\to L)$. Give $B$ its $L$-algebra structure by $h$, and put $S=L[\operatorname{im}b]\subseteq B$, the smallest $L$-subalgebra containing that image. Let $g:\operatorname{Spec}S\to X$ be induced by the restriction of $b\circ a$ to $S$ followed by the affine-spectrum identification. For every $v\in\operatorname{Spec}S$, the canonical extension $\kappa(v)/\kappa(g(v))$ [def-weil-residue-field] is algebraic, meaning that every element satisfies a nonzero polynomial over the base residue field. No injectivity of $b$ or lifting of $v$ to $\operatorname{Spec}B$ is assumed.

proof.text: Let S be the L-subalgebra generated by the image of b:E→B, and fix a prime q of S. Contract q to w in E. The shared-domain equation shows that R→kappa(w) is injective, since its composite to kappa(q) agrees with the injective map through L. Extend to Frac(R)→kappa(w). Uniqueness of fraction-field extension identifies the two maps Frac(R)→kappa(q). Each image of L is therefore algebraic over kappa(w).

source.place: Tag 0F0U, lemma-strictly-henselian, proof before the compatible-model footnote; Tag 0F0X, lemma-interlude-I, second paragraph

proof.text: The images of E in kappa(q) belong to kappa(w), so are algebraic over it; the preceding step treats the scalar images of L. Induction on the algebra generated by these images shows all images of S are integral over kappa(w). Closure under inverses in a field and the fraction representation kappa(q)=Frac(S/q) prove kappa(q)/kappa(w) algebraic.

source.place: Tag 0F0U, lemma-strictly-henselian, proof before the compatible-model footnote; Tag 0F0X, lemma-interlude-I, second paragraph

proof.text: Etaleness gives a separable, hence algebraic, extension at the residue fields of Spec E→Spec Gamma(X). Compose with the affine isomorphism Spec Gamma(X)→X. The standard spectrum residue-field isomorphisms intertwine ideal residue maps with scheme residue maps, as checked on the surjective stalk residue maps. Algebraicity is unchanged by these isomorphisms, and transitivity gives the conclusion.

theorem coefficientImage_residue_algebraic
    (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [IsDomain R]
    (L : Type u) [Field L] [Algebra R L] [Algebra (FractionRing R) L]
    [IsScalarTower R (FractionRing R) L] [Algebra.IsAlgebraic (FractionRing R) L]
    (X : Scheme.{u}) [IsAffine X] (E B : CommRingCat.{u})
    (a : Γ(X, ⊤) ⟶ E) (ha : Etale (Spec.map a))
    (r : CommRingCat.of R ⟶ Γ(X, ⊤)) (b : E ⟶ B) (h : L →+* B)
    (hcomp : r ≫ a ≫ b =
      CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap R L) ≫ CommRingCat.ofHom h) :
    letI : Algebra L B := h.toAlgebra
    let S := Algebra.adjoin L (Set.range b.hom)
    let g := Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom ((b.hom.comp a.hom).codRestrict S
      (fun x ↦ Algebra.subset_adjoin ⟨a.hom x, rfl⟩))) ≫ X.isoSpec.inv
    ∀ v : Spec (.of S),
      @Algebra.IsAlgebraic (X.residueField (g v)) ((Spec (.of S)).residueField v)
        _ _ ((g.residueFieldMap v).hom.toAlgebra)
